edition.tagline: Two cops. One case. Several misunderstandings.
edition.cue: Serve the mains when Lee walks into the Foo Chow restaurant.

s.note: Crisp pastry rolls with cabbage, carrot, shiitake and glass noodles.
s.how: Soak 30g glass noodles in hot water for 5 minutes, drain and cut short. Stir-fry 120g shredded cabbage, 1 grated carrot and 60g finely sliced shiitake in 1 tsp oil for 4 minutes. Add the noodles and 1 tsp light soy sauce, stir 1 minute and cool completely. Divide among 8 spring roll pastry sheets, roll tightly and seal with a paste of 1 tsp flour and 1 tsp water. Fry in neutral oil at 180°C for 3 to 4 minutes until golden. Serve with 40ml sweet chilli sauce.

s.note: Crisp baked wings in hot butter sauce with cooling ranch dip.
s.how: Pat 600g chicken wings dry and season with 1/2 tsp salt. Bake on a rack at 220°C conventional for 45 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp and at least 74°C inside. Melt 25g butter and mix with 35ml hot sauce; toss through the wings. For a cooling ranch dip, mix 80g sour cream, 20g mayonnaise, 1 tbsp chopped chives, 1/4 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp lemon juice. Serve beside the wings.

m.note: Wide rice noodles wok fried with beef, sprouts and spring onion.
m.how: Thinly slice 400g beef rump and marinate for 20 minutes with 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp cornflour and 1 tsp sesame oil. Separate 600g fresh wide rice noodles gently. Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a wok over high heat; stir-fry the beef in two batches for 2 minutes and set aside. Add another 1 tbsp oil and fry the noodles for 2 minutes. Add 150g bean sprouts, 3 sliced spring onions, 1 tbsp dark soy sauce and 1 tbsp light soy sauce. Return the beef and toss over high heat for 2 minutes until piping hot. Serve immediately.

w.note: Thin vanilla cookies folded around paper fortunes while still hot.
w.how: Write 8 fortunes on small clean food-safe paper strips. Whisk 2 egg whites with 50g caster sugar until foamy. Stir in 25g melted butter, 40g plain flour, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract and 1 tbsp water. Spread two thin 10cm circles at a time on a lined tray. Bake at 180°C conventional for 6 minutes until the edges turn golden. Working quickly while hot, place a fortune in each, fold in half and bend over a mug rim into the classic shape. Cool in muffin-tin cups. Repeat for 8 cookies. Remind everyone to remove the paper before eating.

d.note: Ice cold Chinese pale lager, or freshly brewed jasmine tea.
d.how: Chill four 330ml bottles of Chinese pale lager for at least 2 hours. For the tea option, steep 8g jasmine tea in 800ml water at 80°C for 3 minutes, strain and divide among four cups.
